Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nimbus is excited to move forward. Our legal team reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and have a small set of clarifying asks before we sign. I've attached a redline and a current subprocessor export for your reference. High-level items: 

1) Subprocessors: the redline asks that you provide a current, named list of subprocessors and a 30-day notice window when adding any that affect data processing. We also have one specific question about VectorStore Inc. — is that an embeddings vendor used for production inference caching?

2) Data flow / telemetry: We need clarity on what "telemetry" means in the DPA (examples: request/response logs, aggregated latency metrics, crash traces). Nimbus requires a retention cap for any request/response logs tied to customer input.

3) Training / data use carve-out: Our procurement policy requires an explicit prohibition on the use of customer inputs to improve models unless there is an opt-in contract clause. The redline includes language to that effect; please confirm Redwood's position.

Can you loop in product and security to confirm feasibility and help us move to a final form? We are targeting signature by mid-July.

Best,
Sara Liu
Senior Counsel, Nimbus AI

Thanks for the loop-in. Quick product take below (keeping this short so legal/security can confirm):

- VectorStore Inc.: product confirms VectorStore is used for optional embeddings-based caching in our Hosted plan for customers who enable the feature. It's not in the default inference path for all customers; it's only used when the customer opts into "semantic cache". We can agree to name it in a subprocessor list.

- Subprocessor notice window: 30 days for additions is operationally tricky for infra-level updates (we sometimes rotate small helpers), but for any subprocessor that will process customer content (embedding providers, third-party metrics with request-level visibility) we can commit to a 30-day notice. For infra-only changes (e.g., patching helpers), we prefer a shorter operational notification. Suggest language that differentiates "content-processing subprocessors" vs "infra-only helpers".

- Telemetry retention: default retention for request/response logs in Hosted is 30 days; we can offer configurable retention windows (30/90/365) for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private with an MSA addendum. Note: purging request-response logs requires coordination with caching layers and KV stores; Dev, I'd like an estimate on dev effort to support per-customer configurable retention.

I'll add these notes to the shared doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-nimbus-dpa

Thanks — security perspective below. Quoting Sara for visibility: 

On Mon, Jun 29, 2026 at 4:10 PM Sara Liu <sara.liu@teamnimbus.ai> wrote:
> Hi Markus,
>
> Thanks again for the demo last week — Nimbus is excited to move forward. Our legal team reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and have a small set of clarifying asks before we sign...

Short answers: 
- Training / data use: Security (and our privacy policy) do not allow using customer content to train production models unless there is explicit, documented customer consent. We can accept an explicit prohibition on training unless there's an opt-in.

- Subprocessors: We can provide a named list of subprocessors (current as of today) and commit to written notice for any additions that will have access to customer content. We need a contractual process for audit/attestation for any content-processing subprocessor; the attached checklist is what we would expect to share.

- Telemetry & retention: We consider telemetry to include request metadata, aggregated metrics, and request/response logs. For request/response logs we require a documented retention cap; 30 days default for Hosted is acceptable. For enterprise Dedicated/Private customers we can offer extended windows with contractual terms and technical controls (separate storage, encryption keys per customer).

Next step: I recommend we propose the following to Nimbus's counsel in a single reply (keeping posture conservative but negotiable): 
1) Confirm VectorStore is named and is an optional embeddings cache (non-default).
2) Commit to a named subprocessor list plus 30-day notice for content-processing subprocessors; differentiate infra-only helpers with a separate operational notice clause.
3) Confirm prohibition on training on customer inputs absent opt-in.
4) Offer default 30-day request/response retention, with enterprise-configurable windows and KMS/per-customer key options.

If everyone agrees, I'll draft a short security sign-off paragraph they can include in the DPA redline and attach the subprocessor audit checklist. Otherwise propose a 30-minute sync today to close open technical questions.

-Hannah
